title: How mistakes help my brain learn
examples: Why do I keep making mistakes?
Is it okay to get things wrong?

explain.say: Everyone makes mistakes. Mistakes can help you learn. Look at the board. It shows two kinds of thoughts. One is a stuck thought. One is a growing thought.

draw.text: How mistakes help my brain learn

explain.say: Look at the rock. These are stuck thoughts. I can't do it. I always get it wrong. I give up. These thoughts can make you want to stop trying. Have you ever had a stuck thought?
Now look at the seed. These are growing thoughts. I can't do it yet. Mistakes show me how. I will try another way. The word yet means you are still learning. Can you say, I can't do it yet?

Watch how a mistake can help. The first answer says 7 plus 5 is 11. Notice the mistake and count again. 7 plus 3 is 10, and 2 more is 12. Then try again. 7 plus 5 is 12. Can you see how the mistake helped?

faq.a: Mistakes show you what to practise next. Everyone makes them, even experts. They are part of learning.
asks: Tell me about Make a mistake
Is it okay to get it wrong?

faq.q: How do I fix a mistake?
faq.a: Stop and look again. Try a different way, check with an example, or ask for help. Then try again.
asks: Tell me about Find the fix

faq.q: Do mistakes really help my brain?
faq.a: Yes, they can. When you notice a mistake and try again, you practise the right way. Practice helps your brain remember the skill.
Yet means you are still learning it. With practice, it can get easier. I can't ride a bike yet means you are still learning to ride.

faq.q: What if mistakes make me cross?
faq.a: That is okay. Take a breath and a short break. Then come back and try again. A grown-up you trust can help.

facts: Practising a skill, including fixing mistakes, strengthens the brain's connections for that skill.

quiz.say: Aoife gets a sum wrong. Which is a growing thought for her?
quiz.show: Aoife's sum is wrong. Which is a growing thought?
quiz.why: The word yet means Aoife is still learning. With practice, she can get it.

wrong.0: Giving up is a stuck thought that stops her trying.
wrong.2: Always wrong is a stuck thought, and she gets lots of sums right.

quiz.say: Sam says 7 plus 5 is 11. What is the right answer?

wrong.0: 13 is one too many, so count again from 7.
wrong.1: 11 was Sam's first answer, and it is one too few.
